messages.subject: Nimble Data Structure
parts:
I am working on building a model that indexes over 3 dimensions:
origin location: i
destination location: j
time: k

I have a table in R that is set up as:

time_count (k)
origin_kma (i)
destination_kma (j)
y_bar
miles
origin_popDensity
dest_popDensity

My question is: 
How should I set this data up to be used in the model? 
I know I need data for:
y
miles
origin_popDensity
dest_popDensity 

in my model.

I can create a nimMatrix with each of these vectors with dimensions corresponding to the indices, but I do not know how to order my data such that they are input correctly.  ie which dimension should be put in first? Does the matrix fill by row or by column first? 

Any insight would be very helpful.  Thank you!

My Model:
# Model
  for (i in 1:origins){
    for (j in 1:dests){
      for (k in 1:time){
       
      #Primary Prediction Model
      y[i,j,k] ~ dnorm(yhat[i,j,k], y_prec[i,j])
      yhat[i,j,k] <- beta0 + beta_rpm[i,j,k] * miles[i,j,k] + beta_origin_pop * origin_popDensity[i] + beta_dest_pop * dest_popDensity[j] + origin_sp_e[i] + dest_sp_e[j] + temp_e[k] + uncor_e[i,j,k]
      #beta0 is fixed rate flat fee
      #beta0 + origin_sp_e + dest_sp_e + temp_e for a specific lane/date gives you the fixed cost for that lane/date
      #beta_rpm is the lane level rpm (could introduce a temporal aspect to this, but ideally that temp_e error is just moving the overall rate up and down)
     
     
      beta_rpm[i,j,k] ~ dnorm(0,beta_rpm_prec[i,j])
      #May want to investigate the actual sigmas for rates and align this prior
     
     
      }#k
 
    }#j
  }#i
 
  # Intercept
    beta0 ~ dnorm(0, beta0_prec)
    beta_origin_pop ~ dnorm(0, beta_origin_pop_prec)
    beta_dest_pop ~ dnorm(0, beta_dest_pop_prec)
   
  # Spatial Distrubtion
    origin_sp_e[i] ~ dcar_normal(adj_o[1:numNeigh_o],weight_o[1:numNeigh_o],num_o[1:origins], car_o_prec, zero_mean = 1)
    dest_sp_e[i] ~ dcar_normal(adj_d[1:numNeigh_d],weight_d[1:numNeigh_d],num_d[1:dests], car_d_prec, zero_mean = 1)

  # Spatial Weights - Not needed, have it from poly2nb for now
    # weight_o[1:numNeigh_o] <- 1
    # weight_d[1:numNeigh_d] <- 1
   
  # Temporal Distribution - Random Walk prior
    temp_e[1] ~ dnorm(0, temp_prec)
    for(k in 2:time){
      temp_e[k] ~ dnorm(temp_e[k-1], temp_prec)
    }#k
 
  # Priors - May need to tweak these precision prior
  car_o_prec ~ dgamma(2, .5)
  car_d_prec ~ dgamma(2, .5)
  beta0_prec ~ dgamma(2, .5)
  beta_origin_pop_prec ~ dgamma(2, .5)
  beta_dest_pop_prec ~ dgamma(2, .5)
  temp_prec ~ dgamma(2, .5)
  uncor_e_prec ~ dgamma(2, .5)
 
  # Nested Priors
  for (i in 1:origins){
    for(j in 1:dests){
     
      y_prec[i,j] ~ dgamma(2,.5)
      beta_rpm_prec[i,j] ~ dgamma(2, .5)
     
      for(k in 1:time){
       
        uncor_e[i,j,k] ~ dnorm(0, uncor_e_prec)
       
      }#k
    }#j
  }#i

messages.subject: Re: Nimble Data Structure
parts:
Hi Ray,

First you want to make an empty array with the right dimensions, which you can calculate from your table (assuming it's called `dat`):

n_origin <- length(unique(dat$origin_kma))
n_destination <- length(unique(dat$destination_kma))
n_time <- length(unique(dat$time_kma))
y <- array(NA, c(n_origin, n_destination, n_time))

Then, you want to fill this array in the right spots. But I don't know what your response variable is, so I'm just calling it `response`.

for (i in 1:nrow(dat)) {
   y[dat$origin_kma[i], dat$destination_kma[i], dat$time_kma[i]] <- dat$response[i]
}

I hope this is what you were trying to do. I had the same question a few months ago and Ben Augustine helped me get it, so credit to him.

Cheers,

Matt
